Getting Started

For a straightforward first test, choose a single-EXE ABC application and one browse. You can add xSearch without modifying the data dictionary just to hold tags.

First search

  1. Install and register xSearch if needed.
  2. Add the xSearch global extension to the APP, then follow its Start Here tab for the setup sequence.
  3. Open an ABC Browse's Window Designer and place the browse-specific Search control.
  4. Configure the primary file, LIST, Local Queue unique field, and icon field.
  5. Before compiling, open the LIST Formatter for that field and set its icon display to Transparent, not Normal. Normal leaves a visible icon bounding rectangle on nearby rows; Transparent lets the checkmark sit cleanly alongside the column text. See Browse Setup and LIST Icons.
  6. Compile and search for a known value. The matching record should receive a tag icon.
  7. Optionally open the Search control's Appearance tab and enable Highlight tagged rows to color the entire tagged LIST row.

Next step: print or process the selection. Add the relevant xSearch for Report or xSearch for Process extension to an appropriate procedure, configure matching tag storage, and run the procedure normally. A tagged-record prompt can offer to run it on just the selected records. See Reports and Processes Using Tags.

If you want editable dialogs with a coordinated modern appearance, import the Modern window set in Application > Template Utility, or import the familiar Classic set. Both are optional; see Customize xSearch Windows.
